title: Army Equestrian
raw_text:
10-08H. MOS 08H—Army Equestrian (Effective 202603)
   a. Major duties. The Army equestrian supervises or performs ceremonial and related support functions
with military working equids (MWEs) in support of specialized ceremonial detachments and other similar
organizations, activities and units; and advises the commander, the staff, and unit Soldiers on equestrian
matters. Ceremonial equestrian activities support state funerals, military funerals, color guard functions,
historical reenactments, outreach and other activities in support of the Army mission. The Army
equestrian performs all functions in support of the husbandry, training, transportation, recruitment and
disposition of MWEs. Duties for MOS 08H at each level of skill are:
         (1) MOSC 08H2O. Perform care of MWEs to include feeding, watering, grooming, leading,
tacking and untacking, bathing, clipping, health checks, and basic first aid. Perform facilities maintenance
to include stall cleaning and bedding, aisle cleaning, manure removal, resupply of hay, bedding, and
feeds, minor repairs, mowing, and weed removal. Perform maintenance and cleaning of all MWE tack,
equipment, and conveyances. Ride MWEs individually and in postilion in ceremonial military style. Lead
MWEs in ceremonial military style. Maintain fitness of MWEs as directed.
         (2) MOSC 08H3O. Performs duties shown at preceding skill level and provides technical
guidance to subordinate Soldiers in accomplishment of these duties. Acts as squad leader with all typical
and ceremonial responsibilities associated with this position. Drives MWEs in harness. Performs training
of MWEs as directed and under supervision. Transports horses via trailer.
         (3) MOSC 08H4O. Performs duties of and supervises the functions of the preceding skill levels.
Trains MWEs and equestrians directly and through supervision of subordinates. Ensures fitness of
MWEs. Performs staff functions to execute ceremonial missions, support MWEs and Soldiers, and
maintain the organization and its property. Perform platoon sergeant functions with all typical and
ceremonial responsibilities associated with this position.
         (4) MOSC 08H5O. Perform first sergeant functions with all typical and ceremonial responsibilities
associated with this position. Custodian of ceremonial standards and traditions. Advise the commander,
staff, and subordinates on MWE training, fitness, husbandry, and welfare.
         (5) MOSC 08H6O. Supervise duties at the preceding skill levels. Serves as the senior enlisted
equestrian in the Army and senior advisor to the Chief of Army Horses. Ensures MWE welfare and
ceremonial standards are maintained throughout the Army equine enterprise. The SGM ensures the
health of organizations, and development and growth of the future enlisted leaders of Army equestrians.
Provides direct mentorship to Soldiers, provides training oversight to units, and maintains external
relationships, provides readiness oversight.
   b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Army equestrians must possess
the following qualifications:
         (1) A physical demands rating of Significant. (Gray).
         (2) A physical profile of 222221.
         (3) Red/green color discrimination.
         (4) Qualifying scores.
                  (a) A minimum score of 91 in aptitude area ST.
                  (b) A Minimum OPAT Score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) -0140 cm, Seated Power Throw
(PT) - 0400 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0140 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0040 shuttles in
Physical Demands Category in “Significant” (Grey).
         (5) No untreated allergies to animals, hay, dusts, or grasses
         (6) High school diploma/GED.
         (7) No history of a felony conviction.
         (8) A security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award and to maintain the MOS.
         (9) No history of conviction of crimes involving:
              (a) Any weapons/ammunition/explosives/arson charges.
              (b) Any drug activity involving illegal possession, buying, selling or distribution (dealing) of
controlled substances or synthetics.
              (c) Violence against persons, animals or property.
              (d) Sexual misconduct.
           (10) No record of conviction by special or general courts-martial or civilian courts of offenses
listed in AR 27-10 (Military Justice), chapter 24 or otherwise required to register as a sexual offender
under AR 27-10, chapter 24.
          (11) Formal training (completion of a resident course of instruction for MOS 08H conducted under
the auspices of the U.S. Army Equestrian Center of Excellence) mandatory.
     c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASIs associated with all
enlisted MOS).
        (1) None.
     d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
          (1) Table 10-08H-1. Physical requirements.
          (2) Table 10-08H-2. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
